title: Deal Velocity: Risk-managed Playbook (WIP)
body:
Purpose
---
This doc sketches a compact sales enablement play aimed at accelerating close velocity on medium-sized (>$250k ARR) accounts where customers are risk-averse (compliance, latency, and cost predictability). Focus: reduce procurement friction and shorten PoC cycles via a risk-managed offer and prescriptive technical handoff.

Audience
- Platform/AI architects, Head of ML, CTO
- Procurement/Legal (secondary)
- Sales engineers and AMs executing pilots

High-level thesis
- Many qualified buyers stall on procurement or pilot because they can’t validate both quality and predictable unit economics quickly.
- Offer a limited-scope, low-risk pilot: fixed-cost mini-reserved capacity + guarded SLA + isolated data flows. Provide concrete rollback/fallback scripts.

One-line battlecard (for SEs)
- "Short pilot, predictable cost, no vendor lock: 30-day sandbox with pinned model + dedicated reserved slice + canary SLOs — we own the rollback and handoff."

Key play components
1) Offer: "Velocity Slice"
   - 30-day pilot at fixed monthly fee (covers dedicated pool reservation + support hours)
   - Pre-approved model family and quantization profile (to minimize model onboarding time)
   - Access to a trimmed-down console view (read-only for buyer) with latency & cost dashboards

2) Risk mitigations (what to promise and how to deliver)
   - Data: customer data stays in isolated tenant; ephemeral logs by default; provide KMS integration option
   - Reliability: define 3 canary SLO checks that run daily (avg p95 latency, token error rate, throughput headroom) and an auto-fallback plan to an open fallback model if SLOs breach
   - Cost predictability: fixed per-day token cap + alerts, monthly invoice cap hard limit

3) Delivery checklist for SEs (day-by-day cadence)
   - Day 0: Kickoff + NDA/PO checklist, collect test prompts & sample traffic patterns (seq length, qps)
   - Day 1–3: Provision velocity slice, run baseline perf tests, share latency/cost baseline dashboard link
   - Day 4–10: Customer integration window; run guided test script (attached below), collect quality feedback on labeled prompt set (10–50 prompts)
   - Day 11–20: Iterate config (batching, cache TTL, token cap), measure delta; present go/no-go summary
   - Day 21–30: Handoff options: scale to dedicated, migrate to private, or conclude with export of telemetry + artifacts

Slide skeleton (6 slides)
1) Title + customer pain (procurement friction, unpredictable cost)
2) Velocity Slice overview (offer + guarantee)
3) Risk mitigations (data, reliability, cost) — include short table of responsibilities (Redwood vs Customer)
4) Pilot timeline + SE playbook (visual swimlane)
5) How success is measured (quality gates, latency/cost gates, procurement milestone)
6) Next steps / legal + procurement checklist (PO, pilot addendum, support onboarding contact)

Short battlecard cheat sheet (for quick Slack responses)
- Q: "How much will this cost?"
  A: "Fixed pilot fee for 30 days + clear upper cap on tokens. No surprise overages — we stop at the cap and notify."
- Q: "What about my compliance?"
  A: "Tenant isolation, option for KMS, and a short compliance review we can run in parallel — typical turnaround 3–5 business days."
- Q: "What if latency is bad?"
  A: "We ship with a tested kernel/config tuned for your seq length; daily canary checks in pilot. If p95 breaches, we open an escalation and trigger fallback to the verified model family."

SE test script (short)
- Run 3 request classes: short chat (<=64 tokens), structured extraction (<=512 tokens), long completion (<=2048 tokens)
- Send 200 requests of each class during peak window, measure p50/p95/p99, token/sec cost, and error rates
- Capture 20 quality judgments from product owners against labeled prompts

Success metrics (pass/fail gates)
- Quality: >=85% acceptable on labeled prompt set OR no more than 2 regressions from baseline
- Latency: p95 <= target_latency (target specified per account; default 700ms for short chat)
- Cost: pilot avg unit cost <= agreed benchmark OR within 15% of expected
- Procurement: PO received AND legal pilot addendum signed by day 7

Objection playbook (snippets for SEs)
- "We already have infra": "This is focused on accelerating validation with predictable cost and minimal integration time — treat it as a short experiment to de-risk decisions for your infra team."
- "Vendor lock concerns": "Pilot is intentionally scoped with exportable telemetry and a clear off-ramp; we’ll provide an artifacts package and runbook if you choose to leave."

Notes for pricing ops
- Template pilot fee bands by ARR band: <$500k: $15k; $500–2M: $30k; >2M: custom
- Include 8 support hours and onboarding assistance; additional SRE/engineering time billed at T&M

Open questions / risks to iron out
- Legal: need a short pilot addendum (engineering liability/uptime exclusions) — who owns drafting? (ask legal ops)
- Finance: what revenue recognition rules do we use for fixed 30-day pilots? (FP&A)
- Engineering: how much dev time to auto-provision a trimmed console view? (Platform Eng estimate request)

Quick email template to customer (SEs & AMs)
Subject: 30-day risk-managed pilot to validate Redwood for [use-case]
Hi [Name],
Following our call — we can stand up a 30-day Velocity Slice (fixed-cost, dedicated slice, and daily canary checks) to validate latency, quality, and cost predictability. If this sounds good I’ll send a pilot addendum and PO template; provisioning can start within 48–72 hours after PO.
Best,
[SE name]

Play testing plan (internal)
- Week A: run with two existing pilot accounts (one fintech, one HR SaaS) to collect data on provisioning time and typical adjustments
- Week B: incorporate feedback, update slide 3 table with realistic responsibility bullets and update SLO thresholds

Next steps (owners)
- Legal: draft pilot addendum — owner: Maya Lopez — due 2024-12-10
- Finance: confirm billing template & recognition path — owner: Ravi Patel — due 2024-12-05
- Eng: estimate console slice implementation + automation — owner: Ethan Wu — due 2024-12-08
